metadata.title: Genesis on the GPU A World That Proposes Its Own Next Step
metadata.description: We built a geometric world on an RTX 3070 that commits its next state and then proposes again from the state it has become. The world carries 480 flags and 720 overlaps, with THIS or NO readings and a complete witness of their agreements and disagreements. A captured junction event seeds a twelve-flag THIS region bounded by twelve walls. Among 1,924 incidence-generated assignments, exactly one strictly discharges that boundary: the entire region becomes NO, removing all twelve walls and opening none. The world commits this successor as its third link and immediately proposes again on the returned state. The renewed receipts change; no strict successor remains. The same law produces a contrasting result in adjacent-pair diagnostics. All 120 pairs on the refined carrier remain bound, including after ancestor-level offers are added, as do all 30 pairs on the parent carrier. One region dissolves; adjacent pairs persist. These are two outcomes of the same geometric construction, witnessed by exhaustive receipts, replay and withholding controls. Together with renewed proposal on the returned state, they establish an executed world in which settlement and persistent structure arise under one transition law.
metadata.notes: Publication edition v0.5. The eight-page PDF and four supporting run records/seals are exact copies from the public repository release.
